title: "Tap Latency"
toc: false
---

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/apps/shared/tap-along/tap-along.css?v=1">
<script src="/apps/shared/tap-along/tap-latency.js?v=1"></script>

<div class="ta ta-latency">
  <p class="ta-muted">How late each of <a href="/tools/tap-along.html">Tap Along</a>'s buttons lands behind the beat you hear. Use the
  phone and the headphones or speaker you'll mark songs with (Bluetooth adds a lot), turn the ringer on (on an iPhone the silent switch
  mutes this page), and press Start. After four clicks to count you in, tap <b>button 1</b> on the next twelve clicks, then
  <b>button 2</b>, then <b>button 3</b>, the way you'd tap along to a song. Listen to the clicks rather than watching the screen.</p>

  <div class="ta-row">
    <label class="ta-muted">Tempo <select class="ta-bpm"><option>80</option><option selected>100</option><option>120</option></select></label>
    <button type="button" class="ta-go">Start</button>
  </div>
  <div class="ta-cue"></div>
  <div class="ta-results"></div>
  <p class="ta-muted ta-current"></p>
  <p class="ta-muted">The lag is the median of the last ten taps (the first two settle in); the spread shows how steady they were.
  Most people tap a little <i>ahead</i> of a metronome, so a small or negative lag is normal. With Sync, Tap Along takes off
  what the buttons have in common anyway. What matters most is the difference between buttons.</p>

  <div class="ta-pad">
    <div class="ta-keys">
      <button type="button" class="ta-key">1<small>Bar</small></button>
      <button type="button" class="ta-key">2<small>Chord</small></button>
      <button type="button" class="ta-key">3<small>Section</small></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
